text:
Tyler Toffoli's strangest goal of the season went in off an Islanders defender's face on Nov. 9, tying a game San Jose went on to win in a shootout. It was a fitting one for a scorer who has spent more than a decade finding ways for pucks to go in.

At 34, his role is smaller than it used to be. He's averaging 13:16 a night, under 11 minutes in that Islanders game and under 12 in the next, and his own chances have slipped from 1.16 expected goals per 60 last season to 0.91. His legs show it on NHL EDGE: 6th percentile for 20-plus mph bursts.

He's still useful. Five goals and 11 points in 21 games, four on the power play, and our wins-added measure ranks him 60th of 522 skaters, ahead of plenty of younger forwards. The Sharks are better at five-on-five with him on the ice than without him, and his shooting (10.9%) is a touch under his usual, not over.

The recent stretch has been thin, three points in his last ten. On a team building around teenagers, the thing to watch is whether his minutes hold.
